questions.q: A 35-year-old man presents with a painless ulcer on the glans penis with indurated edges and a clean base, accompanied by non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Darkfield microscopy of the serous exudate shows spiral organisms. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Primary syphilis presents with a painless indurated chancre. Darkfield microscopy demonstrates Treponema pallidum spirochetes. Chancroid causes painful ulcers; LGV and donovanosis have different presentations.

questions.q: A 28-year-old farmer from Rajasthan presents with a chronic verrucous plaque on his foot. KOH mount reveals brown, thick-walled, septate fungal cells dividing in multiple planes ('copper penny' or 'Medlar bodies'). What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Chromoblastomycosis is caused by dematiaceous fungi and characterised by Medlar bodies (muriform cells) on histology or KOH. These are brown, round, thick-walled cells dividing by internal septation.

questions.q: A 7-year-old child presents with honey-crusted lesions around the mouth and nose that started as vesicles. Gram stain shows Gram-positive cocci in clusters. Which of the following is the most appropriate first-line topical antibiotic?
questions.exp: Impetigo caused by Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes. Topical mupirocin (2%) is the preferred first-line agent for localised impetigo, with excellent efficacy against Staph aureus including MRSA.

questions.q: A 45-year-old leprosy patient on MDT develops sudden onset of painful erythematous nodules over the body, fever, and joint pain. Nerve function is normal. Which type of lepra reaction is this?
questions.exp: Erythema nodosum leprosum (ENL / Type 2 reaction) occurs in lepromatous and borderline lepromatous leprosy. It is immune-complex mediated (Type III hypersensitivity) and presents with tender erythematous nodules, fever, and systemic features.

questions.q: A 32-year-old woman on hydroxychloroquine for SLE develops a fixed, annular, scaly rash in sun-exposed areas. ANA is negative but anti-Ro/SSA antibodies are strongly positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Subacute cutaneous lupus erythematosus (SCLE) presents with photosensitive annular or papulosquamous lesions. It is strongly associated with anti-Ro/SSA antibodies. ANA may be negative. Drugs like hydroxychloroquine can trigger SCLE.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man presents with tense bullae arising from normal and erythematous skin, sparing the mucous membranes. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposits at the basement membrane zone. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid presents with tense bullae in elderly patients. DIF shows linear IgG and C3 at the DEJ. Autoantibodies target BP180 (type XVII collagen) and BP230. Mucous membrane involvement is uncommon.

questions.q: A 19-year-old student develops multiple grouped vesicles on an erythematous base along a dermatome on one side of the trunk, preceded by 3 days of burning pain. What is the most appropriate antiviral and dosing?
opts: Acyclovir 200 mg 5 times daily for 5 days
Valacyclovir 1000 mg 3 times daily for 7 days
Famciclovir 500 mg twice daily for 7 days
Acyclovir 800 mg 5 times daily for 5 days
questions.exp: Herpes zoster treatment with acyclovir 800 mg 5 times daily for 7 days is standard. Valacyclovir 1000 mg TID or famciclovir 500 mg TID for 7 days are alternatives. Acyclovir 200 mg is the dose for herpes simplex.

questions.q: A 24-year-old woman presents with a 6-month history of comedones, papules, and pustules on her face unresponsive to topical retinoids and antibiotics. She has irregular menstrual cycles. Which investigation is most relevant?
questions.exp: In females with treatment-resistant acne and menstrual irregularities, androgen excess (PCOS or adrenal hyperandrogenism) should be evaluated. Serum free testosterone and DHEA-S are the most informative initial tests to assess androgen sources.

questions.q: A pathology slide shows a tumour with cells arranged in palisading pattern at the periphery of nests, surrounded by a fibromyxoid stroma with cleft artefact between tumour and stroma. Which tumour does this describe?
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma shows peripheral palisading of nuclei with retraction artefact (cleft) between the tumour islands and fibromyxoid stroma. This is a characteristic histological finding distinguishing BCC from other adnexal tumours.

questions.q: A patient on dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops progressive haemolytic anaemia and methaemoglobinaemia despite dose reduction. Testing reveals G6PD deficiency. Which drug can be used as an alternative?
questions.exp: Sulphapyridine is an alternative to dapsone in dermatitis herpetiformis, particularly in patients with G6PD deficiency who cannot tolerate dapsone's haemolytic side effects. A strict gluten-free diet remains the mainstay of long-term management.

questions.q: A 40-year-old woman with a 10-year history of Raynaud's phenomenon develops tight skin over fingers (sclerodactyly), telangiectasias, and calcinosis. Which antibody is most specific for this limited form of systemic sclerosis?
questions.exp: Anti-centromere antibody (ACA) is characteristic of limited cutaneous systemic sclerosis (lcSSc / CREST syndrome). Anti-Scl-70 is associated with diffuse cutaneous SSc with pulmonary fibrosis. Anti-RNA polymerase III is linked to diffuse SSc and renal crisis.

questions.q: A 6-year-old child presents with intensely pruritic vesicles in groups over the elbows, buttocks, and scalp. Skin biopsy shows subepidermal blisters with neutrophils at the tips of dermal papillae. Which investigation confirms the diagnosis?
opts: Direct immunofluorescence showing IgA in dermal papillae
Indirect immunofluorescence showing IgG at DEJ
questions.exp: Dermatitis herpetiformis is confirmed by DIF showing granular IgA deposits in the dermal papillae. It is associated with gluten-sensitive enteropathy. Anti-endomysial IgA is a useful serum marker but DIF is the gold standard.

questions.q: A 55-year-old man from Bihar presents with anaesthetic hypopigmented patches and thickened, tender peripheral nerves. Slit-skin smear is negative. Biopsy shows epithelioid granulomas within nerve fascicles with destruction of the perineurium. What type of leprosy is this?
questions.exp: Tuberculoid leprosy (TT) has high cell-mediated immunity. Biopsy shows epithelioid granulomas that invade and destroy nerve fascicles. Smear is negative (paucibacillary). Patches are well-defined, anaesthetic, and few in number.

questions.q: A sexually active 26-year-old presents with painful, shallow genital ulcers and tender, fluctuant inguinal lymphadenopathy (bubo). Gram stain of bubo aspirate shows Gram-negative coccobacilli arranged in 'school of fish' or 'railroad track' pattern. What is the causative organism?
questions.exp: Chancroid is caused by Haemophilus ducreyi. It presents with painful genital ulcers and tender fluctuant inguinal buboes. The characteristic Gram stain pattern is chains of Gram-negative coccobacilli in 'school of fish' arrangement.

questions.q: A 30-year-old woman develops widespread blistering and skin erosions after 2 weeks on carbamazepine. Skin detachment involves >30% BSA. Nikolsky sign is positive. Which scoring system is used to predict mortality?
questions.exp: SCORTEN (SCORe of Toxic Epidermal Necrosis) is the validated prognostic score for SJS/TEN. It includes age, malignancy, heart rate, BSA involved, BUN, glucose, and bicarbonate. Each parameter scores 1 point; higher scores predict higher mortality.

questions.q: A patient undergoes patch testing. A reaction graded '+' (1+) on Day 4 shows erythema, infiltration, and discrete vesicles. What does this represent immunologically?
questions.exp: Patch testing detects Type IV (delayed-type / T-cell mediated) hypersensitivity, which is the mechanism of allergic contact dermatitis. Reactions are read at 48 and 96 hours. Grading system: + = erythema + infiltration + discrete vesicles.

questions.q: A 42-year-old man presents with well-demarcated silvery scaly plaques on knees, elbows, and scalp. Auspitz sign is positive. Which of the following best describes the basic pathophysiology?
opts: Reduced keratinocyte proliferation with increased apoptosis
Accelerated epidermal turnover (3-4 days) with immune dysregulation driven by Th17 cells and IL-17
Defective filaggrin leading to barrier dysfunction
questions.exp: Psoriasis involves accelerated epidermal turnover reducing from 28 days to 3-4 days. Th17/IL-17 and Th1/TNF-α axes are key. Auspitz sign (pinpoint bleeding on scale removal) reflects dilated papillary dermal capillaries close to surface.

questions.q: A 10-year-old child presents with scalp hair loss in patches with broken hairs ('black dots'), scaling, and mild inflammation. Wood's lamp shows green fluorescence. Which organism is most likely responsible?
questions.exp: Microsporum canis causes tinea capitis (endothrix-ectothrix pattern) and shows bright green fluorescence under Wood's lamp. Trichophyton tonsurans and T. violaceum cause endothrix infection and do not fluoresce. Epidermophyton does not infect hair.

questions.q: A 60-year-old woman presents with periorbital and heliotrope rash, Gottron's papules on knuckles, proximal muscle weakness, and elevated CK. Which antibody is associated with interstitial lung disease in this condition?
questions.exp: Anti-Jo-1 (anti-histidyl tRNA synthetase) is the most common myositis-specific antibody and is associated with the antisynthetase syndrome: ILD, mechanic's hands, arthritis, and Raynaud's. Anti-MDA5 is also linked to ILD (and clinically amyopathic DM). Anti-Mi-2 is associated with classic DM with good prognosis.

questions.q: During Mohs micrographic surgery for a facial BCC, what is the key advantage of horizontal frozen sections compared to conventional vertical bread-loaf sections?
opts: 100% margin assessment of the peripheral and deep margins
Avoidance of need for local anaesthesia
questions.exp: Mohs surgery processes tissue in horizontal (en face) sections that allow examination of the entire peripheral and deep surgical margin (100% margin assessment). Conventional vertical sectioning only samples ~1% of the margin, making it inferior for detecting residual tumour at margins.

questions.q: A 22-year-old woman on isotretinoin for nodulocystic acne complains of excessive dryness. She asks about the mechanism of action. Which of the following is INCORRECT?
opts: It reduces sebaceous gland size and sebum production
It has direct antimicrobial activity against C. acnes
It reduces sebaceous gland ductal epithelial cell proliferation
questions.exp: Isotretinoin works by: reducing sebaceous gland size (up to 90%), normalising follicular keratinisation, reducing sebum secretion, and inhibiting ductal epithelial proliferation. It does NOT have direct bactericidal activity against C. acnes; C. acnes counts fall indirectly due to reduced sebum.

questions.q: A 16-year-old presents with flat-topped violaceous papules on the wrists and oral white reticulate streaks (Wickham's striae). Skin biopsy shows a band-like lymphocytic infiltrate at the DEJ with 'saw-tooth' rete ridges and civatte bodies. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Lichen planus presents with the 6 Ps: purple, pruritic, polygonal, planar papules. Oral Wickham's striae are pathognomonic. Histology: band-like lymphocytic infiltrate, saw-tooth rete ridges, Max-Joseph spaces, civatte bodies (necrotic keratinocytes).

questions.q: A 50-year-old immunocompromised patient develops a rapidly spreading necrotic ulcer on the lower limb after minor trauma. Wound culture grows Pseudomonas aeruginosa. What is this skin manifestation called?
questions.exp: Ecthyma gangrenosum is a skin manifestation of Pseudomonas aeruginosa septicaemia, characterised by necrotic ulcers with grey-black eschar and surrounding erythema. It occurs in immunocompromised patients. The organism invades vessel walls causing ischaemic necrosis.

questions.q: A 25-year-old woman presents with café-au-lait macules (>6, >1.5 cm), axillary freckling, and multiple soft dermal tumours. Which gene mutation underlies this condition?
questions.exp: Neurofibromatosis type 1 (von Recklinghausen disease) is caused by mutations in NF1 gene encoding neurofibromin, a tumour suppressor. Diagnostic criteria include ≥6 CALMs, axillary/inguinal freckling (Crowe's sign), neurofibromas, Lisch nodules, and optic glioma.

questions.q: A patient presents with erythematous scaly patches on sun-exposed areas of the face and 'V' of neck that worsen in summer. ANA is positive at 1:160 with a homogeneous pattern. Anti-dsDNA is negative. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Photosensitivity is one of the ACR/EULAR criteria for SLE. A positive ANA (homogeneous pattern) with systemic features in a young woman with photosensitive rash in the classic malar/V-neck distribution points to SLE. Polymorphous light eruption typically lacks ANA positivity.

questions.q: A 38-year-old HIV-positive patient (CD4 = 85 cells/μL) presents with extensive molluscum contagiosum lesions across the face. What is the most likely explanation for this presentation?
opts: Molluscum is always more severe in adults
CD4 T-cell depletion impairs cell-mediated immunity needed to control poxvirus
Reduced NK cell activity alone explains the severity
questions.exp: Molluscum contagiosum (poxvirus) is normally self-limited due to cell-mediated immunity. In severe immunosuppression (CD4 <200/μL), uncontrolled MCV replication causes giant, numerous, and atypical lesions especially on the face. This is an AIDS-defining presentation.

questions.q: A 29-year-old man presents with erythematous targetoid lesions with concentric rings involving palms, soles, and oral mucosa following a herpes simplex outbreak 10 days ago. What is the pathomechanism?
opts: Direct HSV infection of keratinocytes in the skin lesions
HSV antigen-specific T-cell mediated delayed hypersensitivity in skin
questions.exp: Herpes-associated erythema multiforme (HAEM) is mediated by HSV-specific CD4+ T-cell recruitment to skin where HSV DNA fragments (particularly pol gene) are deposited. This is a Type IV hypersensitivity reaction. HSV is not present in EM lesions but its antigen fragments trigger immune response.

questions.q: A 65-year-old chronic smoker presents with a firm, indurated ulcer on the lower lip with everted edges. Biopsy reveals keratin pearls and intercellular bridges. Regional lymph nodes are enlarged. What is the staging investigation of choice?
opts: Punch biopsy of the lymph node
questions.exp: For squamous cell carcinoma of the lip with regional node involvement, PET-CT is the investigation of choice for staging as it detects locoregional and distant metastases simultaneously. SLNB is used for clinically node-negative high-risk SCC.

questions.q: A 35-year-old man on long-term rifampicin and dapsone for paucibacillary leprosy develops orange discolouration of urine and tears. He is concerned. Which statement is correct?
opts: This indicates haemolysis due to dapsone
This is a harmless side effect of rifampicin causing orange discolouration of body fluids
This suggests hepatotoxicity and rifampicin should be stopped
Clofazimine is responsible for this discolouration
questions.exp: Rifampicin causes harmless orange-red discolouration of urine, tears, sweat, and saliva. Patients should be counselled about this side effect in advance. Clofazimine causes skin discolouration (brownish/reddish-black), not orange tears.

questions.q: A 23-year-old woman develops follicular papules and pustules on her upper back and chest after starting a broad-spectrum antibiotic 3 weeks ago. KOH preparation of the pustule contents shows budding yeast forms. What is the diagnosis?
questions.exp: Malassezia (Pityrosporum) folliculitis presents as monomorphic follicular papulopustules on the upper back and chest, often precipitated by antibiotics that suppress competing bacteria. KOH shows Malassezia yeast (round budding forms). Treatment is topical or systemic azole antifungals.
